description: Most relevant base data around the gross domestic product (GDP): the expenditure identity GDP = consumption + investment + government spending + net exports reproduced for the United States 2023, nominal GDP and population for the United States, Germany and Switzerland 2023 with the derived GDP per capita, and the year-over-year GDP growth derived by the system 'increase' formula through the time dimension (therefore not calc-validated). All GDP figures are nominal; the sources state them in current US dollars and they are converted to euro with the ECB annual average USD per EUR reference rate of the year (2022: 1.0530, 2023: 1.0813), which is stored as a value with the ECB as source. Each word carries a Wikipedia ref plus the cleaned first sentence of the Wikipedia lead as the description so tooltips have text and the ref drives the refresh; the US expenditure components are converted one by one and the stored GDP is their sum (one euro below the rounded direct conversion) so the identity sums exactly.

words.name: GDP
words.description: a monetary measure of the market value of all the final goods and services produced and rendered in a specific time period by a country.

words.name: population
words.description: number of people living in a place

words.name: country
words.description: a distinct part of the world, such as a state, nation, or other political entity.

words.name: United States
words.description: a country primarily located in North America, comprising 50 states.

words.name: Germany
words.description: a country in Central Europe, between the Baltic and North seas and the Alps.

words.name: Switzerland
words.description: a landlocked country at the confluence of Western, Central and Southern Europe.

words.name: consumption
words.description: the use of goods and services by households to satisfy current needs and wants.

words.name: investment
words.description: the commitment of money or resources now in order to gain a future return or benefit.

words.name: spending
words.description: an outlay of money for goods or services

words.name: government
words.description: the system or group of people governing an organized community, generally a state.

words.name: export
words.description: a good or service produced in one country and sold into another country.

words.name: import
words.description: a good or service brought into one country from another.

words.name: nominal
words.description: qualifier: measured at current prices, not adjusted for inflation

words.name: real
words.description: qualifier: adjusted for inflation to constant prices

words.name: inhabitant
words.description: person who lives permanently in a place

triples.name: government spending
triples.description: all spending by the government on consumption, investment, and transfer payments.

triples.name: net exports
triples.description: exports minus imports of goods and services, the trade-balance term of the GDP expenditure identity.

triples.name: gross domestic product
triples.description: total market value of goods and services produced

triples.name: nominal GDP
triples.description: gross domestic product measured at current market prices, not adjusted for inflation.

triples.name: real GDP
triples.description: gross domestic product adjusted for inflation and expressed in constant base-year prices.

triples.name: GDP per capita
triples.description: a country's gross domestic product divided by its population, used as a measure of average economic output per person.

triples.name: GDP growth
triples.description: the increase in a country's gross domestic product from one period to the next.

formulas.name: GDP per capita (formula)
formulas.description: the economic output per inhabitant, which makes the GDP of countries with different population sizes comparable and is a rough indicator of the average material living standard

formulas.name: net exports (formula)
formulas.description: the trade balance of a country, positive if it sells more goods and services abroad than it buys, negative for a trade deficit

formulas.name: GDP (expenditure)
formulas.description: the expenditure approach to the gross domestic product: everything produced in a country is bought either by households, by investors, by the government or by foreign customers net of imports
